agenda: The situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Greece’s primary objective as penholder is to secure the smooth 12-month renewal of EUFOR ALTHEA’s executive Chapter VII mandate, ensuring continued security and stability in the Western Balkans and supporting the European Union's vital stabilization role. To prevent a Russian veto and preserve Council consensus, Greece maintains a strictly technical and focused draft modelled on resolution 2795 (2025). We anticipate potential friction if Western partners push to reinsert references to the High Representative or Euro-Atlantic integration, which Russia firmly rejects in the mandate text.

messages.Bahrain: The Kingdom of Bahrain fully supports the renewal of the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months, as it plays an indispensable role in maintaining peace, security, and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We commend the penholder, Greece, for presenting a clean and balanced text that preserves Council unity on this critical mission. Bahrain is prepared to vote in favour of the draft resolution as presented.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA to help maintain peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement and respecting the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the country. We appreciate Greece's balanced approach as penholder in maintaining the established, consensus-based language from previous years. China is ready to support the draft resolution as currently drafted.
messages.Colombia: Colombia fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholder to renew the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. We recognize the vital role played by EUFOR ALTHEA and the NATO presence in maintaining stability, security, and peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina in full accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement. We hope the Council can adopt this essential and well-established renewal by consensus.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. Maintaining this stabilization force is vital for preserving peace, security, and territorial integrity in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region. We commend the penholder for presenting a balanced text that preserves Council consensus and we are prepared to vote in favor of the resolution as drafted.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the draft resolution circulated by Greece renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for a further twelve months. EUFOR ALTHEA continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment and safeguarding stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Preserving the established, streamlined text ensures Council unity and the seamless continuation of this vital mission.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution circulated by Greece renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. The operation continues to play an indispensable role in safeguarding stability, sovereignty, and territorial integrity in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We favor adopting this well-established, consensual text without modification to preserve Council unanimity.
messages.Latvia: Latvia fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. The mission remains essential to preserving a safe and secure environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as supporting stability in the wider Western Balkans. We commend Greece for its leadership as penholder and favor adopting the text as drafted.
messages.Liberia: Liberia expresses its full support for the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for a further period of twelve months. The continued presence and mission of EUFOR ALTHEA, in cooperation with NATO, remain vital to maintaining stability, security, and peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region. We thank Greece for circulating this streamlined and balanced text and look forward to its consensus adoption.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for a further twelve months. We commend the penholder for presenting a clean and balanced text that preserves Council unity and ensures the continued stabilizing presence of the multinational force. Pakistan reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution circulated by Greece renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. The multinational stabilization force plays an indispensable role in maintaining peace, stability, and security in Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Dayton Peace Agreement. We endorse the draft as presented and look forward to its prompt adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for a further twelve months as circulated by the penholder. We appreciate that the draft retains a strictly technical and balanced character, maintaining focus on the implementation of Annexes 1-A and 2 of the Dayton Peace Agreement without introducing divisive political language or references to the illegitimate High Representative. We expect EUFOR ALTHEA to continue discharging its mandate neutrally and impartially, strictly refraining from interfering in the domestic political processes of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. The multinational stabilization force continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment and preserving peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We commend Greece for penning this balanced text and stand ready to support its adoption as circulated.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks Greece for circulating this draft text renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA, which remains vital to maintaining peace, stability, and security in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We fully support the continuation of the force's mandate and NATO's presence under Chapter VII as drafted. We favor preserving the agreed language to ensure a swift, unanimous adoption without unnecessary complications.
messages.United States of America: The United States fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for an additional twelve months. Operation EUFOR ALTHEA, operating in close cooperation with NATO Headquarters Sarajevo, remains indispensable for safeguarding peace, security, and the territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina under the Dayton Peace Agreement. We commend Greece for maintaining the streamlined, proven text to ensure the Council's continued unanimous support.

steps.summary: All Council members expressed full support for the draft resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR ALTHEA for a period of twelve months, with no amendments proposed. As penholder, Greece maintains the agreed, balanced text unchanged to preserve Council unanimity. The resolution is set for unanimous adoption.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted, which renews the authorization of the multinational stabilization force in Bosnia and Herzegovina (EUFOR ALTHEA). We support the continued constructive role played by EUFOR ALTHEA in helping to maintain peace, security and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Bosnia and Herzegovina is an important country in the Western Balkans. Maintaining its peace, stability and development is in the fundamental interest of all ethnic groups in the country and conforms to the shared expectations of the international community and countries in the region. China's position on the issue of Bosnia and Herzegovina has always been consistent and clear. We consistently respect the sovereignty, independence, national unity and territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and support its people in independently choosing their own development path in accordance with their national conditions.

The Dayton Peace Agreement is the cornerstone of peace and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. China hopes that all parties, the two entities and the three constituent peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina will put the overarching interests of the country and its people first, enhance mutual trust, foster national unity, and resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation on an equal footing, so as to achieve enduring political stability, national reconciliation and sustainable socioeconomic development.

The international community, in assisting Bosnia and Herzegovina, should uphold an objective, balanced and prudent approach, respect the ownership and leadership of the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and avoid imposing external solutions or taking unilateral actions that could aggravate ethnic divisions and tensions. China stands ready to work with the international community to continue playing a constructive role in promoting peace, stability and long-term prosperity in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider Western Balkans region.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Denmark:
Mr. President,

Denmark welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR Operation Althea for another twelve months. We thank Greece for its leadership and dedicated efforts as penholder.

The unanimous renewal of EUFOR Althea reflects this Council’s continued and resolute commitment to stability, peace and security in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider Western Balkans. EUFOR Althea plays an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment and in supporting the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement, working in close and effective cooperation with NATO.

Denmark reaffirms its steadfast and unequivocal support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a single, sovereign and independent state. We also reiterate our firm support for the Office of the High Representative and its mandate to oversee the civilian aspects of the Peace Agreement.

We remain concerned by divisive, nationalist and secessionist rhetoric and actions that undermine the state institutions, constitutional framework and stability of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Such actions are unacceptable and run counter to the Dayton Peace Agreement and the country's aspirations. We urge all political leaders to refrain from provocative measures and instead engage in constructive dialogue to strengthen the functionality of state institutions.

Bosnia and Herzegovina belongs in the European family. Following the historic decision to open accession negotiations, we urge the authorities and political leaders of Bosnia and Herzegovina to seize the current momentum and pursue the necessary reforms, particularly in the rule of law, the judiciary and fundamental rights. Denmark stands ready to continue supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina on its European path for the benefit and prosperity of all its citizens.

Thank you.
after.France:
France welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the European Union military operation EUFOR ALTHEA for a further twelve months. We thank Greece for its efforts as penholder in facilitating this outcome.

Since 2004, the European Union has played a crucial role in maintaining stability and security in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region through EUFOR ALTHEA. Operating under a mandate from this Council and in accordance with the Dayton-Paris Peace Agreement, EUFOR ALTHEA continues to provide an indispensable contribution to a safe and secure environment, deterring destabilizing actors and reassuring all communities. France remains fully committed to this operation.

As a witness to the Dayton-Paris Peace Agreement, France reaffirms its unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We call on all political leaders to reject divisive rhetoric and any initiatives that undermine the constitutional order and the functionality of state institutions. 

France also reiterates its full support for the High Representative and his mandate. 

Finally, France remains resolutely committed to Bosnia and Herzegovina's European path. We encourage its leaders to pursue the necessary reforms to strengthen the rule of law, democracy, and economic development, in the interest of all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina and for the shared European future of the region.
after.Greece:
Greece welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the authorization of the European Union military operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR-Althea, for another twelve months. As the penholder of this resolution, we express our sincere appreciation to all members of the Security Council for their constructive engagement and unanimous support throughout the process.

Since its deployment in 2004, EUFOR-Althea has played an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina and preserving peace and stability across the Western Balkans. Today's unanimous decision sends a clear and unified message of the Council’s continued commitment to security and stability in the region.

Greece reaffirms its unwavering support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina, based on the General Framework Agreement for Peace and its annexes. We believe that the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina lies within the European Union. Rooted in the principles of the 2003 Thessaloniki Agenda, our vision remains firmly focused on peace, reconciliation, good-neighbourly relations, and the European integration of the Western Balkans.

As a long-standing troop-contributing country to EUFOR-Althea and a regional partner, Greece remains steadfast in its dedication to supporting Bosnia and Herzegovina on its path toward lasting stability, unity, and prosperity.
after.Latvia:
Latvia welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of EUFOR Operation Althea for another year. We thank Greece as the penholder for its leadership and efforts in guiding the Council to this consensus.

EUFOR Althea, acting in close cooperation with the NATO Headquarters in Sarajevo, remains an indispensable pillar of stability, playing a vital role in maintaining a safe and secure environment and supporting the implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement. Today’s unanimous vote sends a clear signal of the international community's shared commitment to peace and security in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider Western Balkans.

Latvia reiterates its unwavering support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a single, united state within its internationally recognized borders. 

We remain deeply concerned by persistent divisive, inflammatory, and secessionist rhetoric and actions that challenge the authority of state institutions and undermine the Dayton Peace Agreement. Such actions risk derailing the progress achieved over the past three decades and jeopardizing the country’s stability. We call on all political leaders in Bosnia and Herzegovina to refrain from provocative rhetoric and to engage constructively in dialogue and genuine reconciliation.

Latvia also reaffirms its full support for the Office of the High Representative and its mandate, which remains essential to overseeing the civilian implementation of the Peace Agreement until the 5+2 agenda has been fully fulfilled. 

Following the European Council's historic decision to open accession negotiations, Bosnia and Herzegovina has a clear European future. We encourage all political stakeholders to seize this momentum, prioritize meaningful democratic and rule-of-law reforms, and advance the country’s integration into the European family for the benefit and prosperity of all its citizens.

Thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the authorization of EUFOR ALTHEA for another year. We thank the penholder, Greece, for steering the consultations that led to the unanimous renewal of this important mandate. 

Pakistan enjoys deep-rooted, warm, and fraternal ties with Bosnia and Herzegovina and its people. Our commitment to the peace, stability, and prosperity of Bosnia and Herzegovina remains steadfast and enduring. 

We reiterate our full and resolute support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and unity of Bosnia and Herzegovina within its internationally recognized borders. The General Framework Agreement for Peace—the Dayton Peace Agreement—together with the constitutional architecture and State institutions established under it, remains the bedrock of peace and stability in the country.

In this context, the presence of EUFOR ALTHEA continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment, building confidence, and supporting peace implementation in cooperation with NATO. Today’s unanimous adoption reflects the Council’s shared conviction regarding the vital contribution of EUFOR ALTHEA to regional stability.

We note with concern the persistent political challenges and polarising narratives that threaten to undermine the functioning of State institutions. We call on all political leaders and parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina to refrain from inflammatory rhetoric, unilateral actions, and secessionist tendencies. Lasting peace and progress can only be achieved through constructive dialogue, mutual respect among all constituent peoples and others, and a collective commitment to strengthen democratic institutions and the rule of law.

Pakistan will continue to support all efforts aimed at consolidating peace, fostering reconciliation, and ensuring a peaceful, unified, and prosperous future for all the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which renews for a further twelve months the authorization of the European Union military operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR ALTHEA.

We welcome the representatives of Bosnia and Herzegovina and other participating delegations present with us today, and we thank Greece for its efforts as penholder on this file.

More than three decades since the signing of the General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the maintenance of peace and stability in the country remains a vital objective for the region and for the international community. Panama reiterates its firm and unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

In this context, EUFOR ALTHEA continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment, providing reassurance to all communities, and preventing the resurgence of instability. Its ongoing presence, in close cooperation with NATO, serves as an essential pillar of deterrence and peace consolidation.

Panama also reaffirms the crucial importance of the institutions and mechanisms established under the Dayton framework, including the Office of the High Representative, in upholding the constitutional order and the rule of law. We remain concerned by divisive and secessionist rhetoric and actions that challenge state institutions and undermine social cohesion. We call on all political leaders in Bosnia and Herzegovina to refrain from inflammatory discourse, engage in constructive dialogue, and work collectively toward strengthening state-level institutions and advancing the reforms necessary for the prosperity and democratic development of all its citizens.

Panama stands ready to continue supporting all multilateral efforts aimed at consolidating long-term peace, reconciliation, and stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the wider region.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation supported the adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the European Union military operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR-Althea, for an additional 12-month period.

Our position on this matter is consistent and principled. We proceed from the understanding that EUFOR-Althea continues to perform a purely stabilizing function in strict accordance with the military aspects of the General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina—the Dayton Agreement. It is of fundamental importance that the mission maintain an objective, balanced, and politically neutral stance, refraining from any interference in the domestic political processes of Bosnia and Herzegovina or taking sides in inter-ethnic issues. 

The Dayton Peace Agreement remains the bedrock of peace, stability, and constitutional order in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its core principles—the equal rights of the three constituent peoples (Bosniaks, Croats, and Serbs) and the broad constitutional powers of the two entities, the Republika Srpska and the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina—must be scrupulously respected. Any external attempts to dismantle this architecture, erode entity competencies, or centralize the state against the will of its peoples are dangerous, counterproductive, and fraught with destabilization.

We must once again draw the Council's attention to the deeply flawed and illegitimate role played by the external protectorate in the country. The post of High Representative remains vacant, as the appointment of Mr. Christian Schmidt was never endorsed by the Security Council through an appropriate resolution. Consequently, his arbitrary decisions, use of the illegitimate "Bonn powers," and interference in the legal and political systems of Bosnia and Herzegovina have no legal force and serve only to exacerbate tensions and undermine genuine internal dialogue among the Bosnian parties themselves. The sovereign future of Bosnia and Herzegovina belongs solely to its peoples, without uninvited foreign tutelage, external dictation, or illegitimate interference.

Thank you.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of the European Union-led multinational stabilization force, EUFOR ALTHEA, for a further period of twelve months. We thank the penholder, Greece, for steering the consultations leading to this outcome.

Our vote in favour reflects Somalia’s steadfast support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as our enduring commitment to peace and stability in the Western Balkans.

EUFOR ALTHEA continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment and in supporting the implementation of the military aspects of the General Framework Agreement for Peace. Its presence remains vital in preventing tensions and fostering conditions conducive to political stability and institutional progress.

Somalia firmly believes that the General Framework Agreement for Peace remains the bedrock of stability in Bosnia and Herzegovina. We urge all political leaders and stakeholders to reaffirm their commitment to the Dayton Peace Agreement, uphold the country’s constitutional framework, and refrain from divisive rhetoric and unilateral actions that could undermine state institutions or escalate tensions.

Sustainable peace can only be achieved through genuine reconciliation, inclusive political dialogue, and consensus-building. We encourage all parties to work constructively together to address political and socio-economic challenges for the benefit of all the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

In conclusion, Somalia reaffirms its continued support for Bosnia and Herzegovina on its path toward lasting peace, stability, and prosperity.

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the mandate of EUFOR-Althea for a further twelve months, and I thank Greece for its diligent work as penholder on this text.

EUFOR-Althea continues to play an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its continued presence, alongside NATO’s vital support, sends a clear signal of the international community’s enduring commitment to peace and stability in the country and the wider region.

The United Kingdom’s commitment to Bosnia and Herzegovina is steadfast. We remain fully dedicated to supporting its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and constitutional order as established under the Dayton Peace Agreement. 

In that regard, we reiterate our full support for the High Representative, Christian Schmidt, and the use of the Bonn powers where necessary to protect the Dayton structures and preserve stability. Any attempts to undermine the High Representative, the Constitutional Court, or State-level institutions are unacceptable and threaten the hard-won peace of the past three decades.

Divisive, secessionist rhetoric and actions only harm the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina and distract from the essential reforms needed to improve governance, strengthen the rule of law, and advance the country’s Euro-Atlantic integration. We urge all political leaders across both entities to move away from provocative actions, respect the rule of law, and work constructively together for the benefit of all the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
after.United States of America:
The United States welcomes the Security Council’s unanimous reauthorization of the mandate for the European Union military operation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, EUFOR-Althea. We thank Greece for its leadership as penholder on this resolution, and we extend our deep appreciation to the European Union and troop-contributing countries for their continued commitment to regional stability.

The unanimous adoption today demonstrates our shared recognition that EUFOR-Althea, operating in cooperation with the NATO Headquarters presence, plays an indispensable role in maintaining a safe and secure environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Rooted in the Dayton Peace Agreement, EUFOR-Althea remains vital to supporting the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and multi-ethnic character of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States’ commitment to the Dayton Peace Agreement and to the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina remains steadfast. We continue to support a peaceful, democratic, and prosperous Bosnia and Herzegovina fully integrated into the Euro-Atlantic community. 

Achieving that future requires political leaders to turn away from divisive actions and focus on the hard work of governance and reform. The United States remains deeply concerned by persistent ethno-nationalist rhetoric, threats of secession, and actions aimed at undermining State-level institutions and the constitutional order. Such efforts violate the Dayton Peace Agreement, threaten the stability of the entire region, and obstruct the meaningful economic and rule of law reforms that the citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina want and deserve.

We also reiterate our full support for the Office of the High Representative and High Representative Christian Schmidt. The High Representative continues to play an essential role in overseeing the civilian implementation of the Dayton Peace Agreement until the 5+2 agenda is fulfilled. Attempts to delegitimize or obstruct the High Representative’s mandate are counterproductive and unacceptable.

The United States calls on all political leaders in Bosnia and Herzegovina to engage in constructive dialogue, reject divisive and destabilizing tactics, and work together to strengthen the country's democratic institutions. The United States will continue to stand with all those who are dedicated to securing a peaceful, stable, and prosperous future for all the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Thank you.
